lesson.menu_desc: Asking for directions in New York and understanding the answer -- imperatives and prepositions of place
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 7 -- Where Is the Subway?
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Carlos Henrique Rodrigues | Lesson 7 -- Where Is the Subway?
lesson.grammar_point: imperatives and prepositions of place (turn left, go straight, next to, across from)

listenings.text: Good morning. The museum is not far. Walk out of the hotel and turn left. Go straight for three blocks. At the corner with the bank, turn right. That is 53rd Street. Walk one more block. The museum is on your left, next to a small coffee shop. It is across from a big bookstore. It is about ten minutes on foot. You don't need a taxi.

Manhattan is easy, I promise. Streets go from east to west, and they have numbers: 42nd Street, 57th Street. Avenues go from north to south: Fifth Avenue, Sixth Avenue. A short block, from one street to the next, is about one minute on foot. A long block, between two avenues, is about three minutes. And the subway? There is a station on the corner of many streets. It is fast. Don't take a taxi at five o'clock!

extra_audio.text: Carlos and his wife are lost in Manhattan. Carlos says: Excuse me, where is the subway? A woman says: Go straight for four blocks. Then she says: Turn left on 59th Street. Carlos asks her to say it again, slowly. They find the park, across from the station.
